text.p: Aurex Resources Corp said on Tuesday that it has a deal to acquire U.S.-based Cobre Mining Co through an amalgamation and share exchange.
Cobre will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Aurex.
Aurex said it would pay US$46.5 million for the Cobre shares by issuing 124 million Aurex shares at US$0.375 per share.
Aurex will change its name to Cobre Mining Co Inc when the deal has closed and will consolidate its share capital on a 10 to 1 basis.
Before closing, Cobre will raise an additional US$50 million through a special warrants equity financing, Aurex said.

The proceeds will be used to retire about US$36 million of debt and agreements between Glencore Ltd and Cobre, with the balance going to fund Cobre's mill expansion and exploration program, Aurex said.
After the share consolidation and equity financing, there will be about 28.9 million shares of Cobre Mining Co outstanding.
Cobre owns the Continental copper mine near Silver City, Mexico. Cobre produced more than 52 million pounds of copper in the first nine months of 1996 at a cash cost of US$0.77 per pound.
Cobre has proven and probable reserves totalling about 1.8 billion pounds of copper.
Aurex shareholders are to meet no later than March 1997 to vote on the deal.
